To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) top managers' transformation leadership was significantly associated with staff attitudes toward EBs; (2) staff attitudes were significantly associated with middle managers' implementation of leadership; and (3) middle managers' implementation was significantly associated with delivery of EBPs.

top managers' transformation leadership is associated with middle managers' implementation of leadership which, in turn, is associated with attitudes toward EBPs which, in turn are associated with delivery of EBPs by frontline staff.

top managers' transformation leadership influences staff attitudes toward evidence-based practices through middle managers' implementation behaviors, which ultimately affects delivery of evidence-based practices by staff.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how leadership at multiple levels of an organizational hierarchy affects the implementation of innovative practices.
advancing theory on the multilayered role of leadership in implementation and has implications for developing a leadership approach to implementation.
the multilevel influence of leadership on staff attitudes and implementation of EBPs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the findings partially supported our theory-driven multilevel leadership theory model.
our study shows the importance of top managers' and middle managers' leadership in influencing frontline staff attitudes and behaviors toward EBPs.

top managers' transformation leadership influences staff attitudes toward evidence-based practices through middle manager implementation leadership, and that this relationship is mediated by middle managers' transformational and transactional leadership.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
leadership is important in health care implementation, and that leadership is multilevel.
top managers' transformation leadership is associated with middle managers' implementation behaviors, which, in turn, influence staff attitudes and implementation of EBPs.
top managers' transformation leadership influences staff attitudes toward EBPS, but only when middle managers' implementation competencies and leadership are in place.
The main takeaway from our work is that
leadership development programs should include training on implementation leadership for middle managers and on how to build a culture of innovation for top managers.
top managers can influence staff attitudes toward EBs and their implementation through middle managers' implementation skills.
top managers' leadership is important, not just for frontline staff, but also for middle managers who are critical to implementation.
